newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/4 to 3/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/4 to 3/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices tracked U.S. Treasuries higher Monday, finishing up 1/4 to 3/8 ahead of Tuesday's $324 million Washington Public Power Supply System refunding deal.
"The market is again getting very thin, at least the long end," one trader said. "WPPSS only goes out to 2012."
The trader judged the market up "a solid quarter of a point," but said he wouldn't give it any more than that. He described the session as "a typical, quiet Monday."
A municipal analyst said high-grade issues rose 1/4, while dollar bonds added 1/4 to 3/8.
Activity was light, he said.

"I think we breathed kind of a sigh of relief when the Treauries regained their losses on Friday," the analyst said. "And then we've got some very interesting competitive issues, (and) a couple of interesting negotiated issues people can get their teeth in."
In competitive action Monday, Smith Barney Inc won $67 million Colorado Springs, Colo., bonds at a true interest cost of 5.862 percent.
The firm reoffered 2023 term bonds at a 5.75 percent yield. The 2025 terms were not formally reoffered.
"I thought the pricing was good," the analyst said. He described pricing as "strong."
Smith Barney said later it had a $7.7 million balance.
On the negotiated side, William R Hough & Co tentatively priced $142.2 million Sunrise, Fla., utility bonds at a top yield of 5.938 percent in 2026.
"Sunrise looked okay to me," the analyst said. "I thought it was right on target...I didn't assess the zeroes, but the term bonds were certainly there."
Clark Wagner, chief investment officer at First Investors Management Co, said First Investors put in for some Sunrise bonds.
"It looked attractive for Florida paper," he said, prior to the deal's repricing.
Late in the day, William R Hough repriced the deal, lowering yields in several maturities but leaving the top yield unchanged.
As for the WPPSS deal, "it's a little short for us," Wagner said. Goldman Sachs & Co is expected to price the deal Tuesday.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed up 17/32 at 111-31/32, with December T-bonds 15/32 higher at 107-7/32. The MOB spread was 152 ticks.
In the cash governments market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 14/32 at 96 to yield 7.07 percent.

On the economic front, the market receives data on August producer prices Thursday and on August consumer prices Friday. Economists polled by Reuters expect a 0.1 percent rise in PPI both overall and for the core rate, which excludes food and energy. They see a 0.2 percent rise in CPI, both overall and in the core rate.
--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655
